cross_references.relationship: COORDINATED REGIME — §17500 violation is per se unlawful under §17200's 'unlawful' prong; §17200's 'fraudulent' prong independently covers misleading conduct without needing §17500's knowledge element. Always plead both. UCL remedies (injunction + restitution) stack with §17535 remedies.

COMMON LAW SUPPLEMENT — §17500 false advertising + §1709/§1710 intentional misrepresentation are separate causes of action on the same dealer fraud facts. §1709 requires intent; §17500 requires only 'should know.' Plead both: §17500 is easier to prove; §1709 opens §3294 punitive damages pathway via §3343 out-of-pocket damages.

SEPARATE TRACK — Song-Beverly covers warranty breach; §17500 covers deceptive advertising in the sale transaction. Both can proceed against a dealer on the same vehicle. §1794(c) civil penalty for willfulness is separate from §17500 restitution. False advertising about warranty coverage = §17500 violation + §1790 warranty breach simultaneously.

COLLECTION SIDE — §17500 covers false representations in the sale transaction; Rosenthal Act covers false representations in subsequent debt collection. Yo-yo financing: §17500 applies at point of sale (false financing term representations); if dealer/finance company then collects on an inflated rate using deceptive communications, Rosenthal Act applies to the collection conduct.
